Question ID: JOUR_U04_L04_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.JOUR.MED.04

Source: Topic: Should the school create a phone-free lunch area? Argument A: The school should create a phone-free lunch area because many students need a place to talk without screens taking over the table. A guidance counselor says some students report feeling ignored when everyone around them is scrolling. A pilot table in the media center attracted twenty students during one week, and several said it helped them meet classmates. Supporters say the area would be optional, so students who want to use phones at lunch could still sit elsewhere. Argument B: The school should not create a phone-free lunch area because lunch is one of the few flexible times students have during the day. Many students use phones to check family messages, manage club reminders, or finish quick tasks. A student council survey found that sixty-eight percent of respondents opposed lunch phone restrictions. Opponents argue that a separate area may divide students instead of teaching respectful conversation habits for all tables. Question 01: Which choice accurately compares the two claims?

answer.text: Both arguments claim that phones should be banned from the entire school.
